summary: A whimsical diary-style reflection by a frequent business traveler on Zenith Innovations' "Accommodation and Meal Expense Guidelines." It walks through pre-trip approval, hotel selection, meal allowances, receipts and reimbursement, prohibited expenses, and personal stay extensions. The narrator concludes that the policy acts as a guiding lighthouse rather than a cage.
one_line: A diary-style narrative of Zenith Innovations' travel accommodation and meal expense policy, from pre-trip approval to reimbursement and personal extensions.
key_facts: The guidelines are Zenith Innovations' "Accommodation and Meal Expense Guidelines", written about from the perspective of a seasoned traveler, the "Zenith Road Warrior".
Trip requests require pre-trip approval from the budget committee.
The accommodation rule is paraphrased as "Thou shall seek comfort, but not opulence."
Zenith Innovations caps nightly hotel rates, which the narrator treats as a challenge to get the best "bang for our buck."
Meals are covered by a daily allowance spanning breakfast to dinner, with occasional snacks.
The meal guidance is summarized as "Satiate thy hunger, but watch the bottom line."
Zenith's reimbursement system is paperless; travelers upload photos of their receipts.
Mini-bars and in-room movies are forbidden extravagances under the policy.
Zenith allows travelers to extend a stay for personal time at their own expense; personal charges remain personal.
The narrator sees the extension allowance as evidence of Zenith's awareness of work-life balance.
The narrator likens the guidelines to lighthouses that guide rather than fences that cage.
